summary: A satellite and space seminar [adopted eleven recommendations](2026-07-27-agp-gabon-communications-spatiales-11-recommandations-souverainete) in July 2026 and confirmed a hybrid fibre-and-satellite model, without drafting the strategy.
developments:
The Libreville seminar closed with eleven recommendations and confirmation of a hybrid model combining fibre and satellite, and recommended an integrated national strategy rather than producing one ([seminar recommendations](2026-07-27-agp-gabon-communications-spatiales-11-recommandations-souverainete)).

No delivery date, budget line or drafting owner is named ([seminar account](2026-07-29-gabon-advances-digital-sovereignty-with-national-satellite-seminar)), and the base holds no broadband plan, coverage target or national digital strategy document of any kind.

summary: [Loi n 025/2023](2023-07-15-gabon-loi-025-2023-protection-donnees-personnelles) has bound from publication on 15 July 2023, with article 219 setting no grace period and no transitional window.
developments:
The statute was published in the gazette of 15 July 2023 and took effect at once, article 219 allowing no transition ([Loi n 025/2023](2023-07-15-gabon-loi-025-2023-protection-donnees-personnelles)).

It repeals contrary prior provisions of the 2020 ordinance, and the base does not establish whether the funding levy that ordinance created was carried forward ([the 2020 ordinance](2020-03-27-gabon-ordonnance-00002-pr-2020-protection-donnees)).

The gazetted text of the founding 2011 statute is not held, so the earlier baseline is read only through the amending instruments.

progress: No change, an outright biometric prohibition standing with its own derogation route defective
summary: Article 75 [prohibits biometric processing outright](2023-07-15-gabon-loi-025-2023-protection-donnees-personnelles) and article 76 cross-references its derogation to the wrong article, leaving the route defective.
developments:
The prohibition is absolute on the face of the statute, and the derogation that would open it points to the article on children's data rather than to the prohibition it is meant to qualify ([Loi n 025/2023](2023-07-15-gabon-loi-025-2023-protection-donnees-personnelles)).

That is recorded as a defect in the gazetted text rather than read as intended, and it stands unamended against an identity card, a biometric civil registry and an airport passenger-data system all in operation.

summary: The [data protection authority](2026-06-10-gabon-datacenter-readiness-apdpvp-compliance) has two dated acts on record, a supervised file destruction and a pre-commissioning clearance for the national data centre.
developments:
The authority supervised the destruction of unsuccessful bidders' files on 20 January 2026 ([file destruction](2026-01-20-gabon-apdpvp-procurement-data-destruction)) and announced pre-commissioning compliance clearance for the national data centre on 9 June 2026 after several months of accompaniment ([compliance clearance](2026-06-10-gabon-datacenter-readiness-apdpvp-compliance)).

It was created by article 7 of the 2023 statute and is funded by a levy of 1,000 FCFA per person per year split 40 per cent to the state and 60 per cent to the authority ([funding levy](2020-03-27-gabon-ordonnance-00002-pr-2020-protection-donnees)).

No register of authorisations, declarations or sanctions is published, and both acts are known only from press accounts.

summary: [Loi n 027/2023](2025-06-01-gabon-aninf-secbom-cybersecurity) on cybersecurity and cybercrime is in force from July 2023, its text not held.
developments:
The statute appeared in the same gazette issue as the data-protection law, of 15 July 2023, and is named as present in the captured issue without being reproduced in it ([gazette issue](2023-07-15-gabon-loi-025-2023-protection-donnees-personnelles)).

It reaches the base through the security agency's own account of its work rather than through the instrument ([agency account](2025-06-01-gabon-aninf-secbom-cybersecurity)).

No article text, implementing decree, prosecution or sanction under it is held.

summary: The identity framework [rests on two named texts](2025-09-16-gabon-digital-identity-governance-milestone), a law on the personal identification number and one on the civil registry centre, neither with a date.
developments:
Both texts are named as the legal basis of the national digital identity system, with no adoption, promulgation or gazette date for either ([framework](2025-09-16-gabon-digital-identity-governance-milestone)).

They were named again in the stocktake of legal identity projects, which lists three separate systems resting on them ([legal identity stocktake](2025-06-23-gabon-legal-digital-id-three-projects)).

Neither text has a number, date or gazette reference on file, so the identity card, the biometric register and the digital identity system all operate on a basis the base cannot read.

summary: An [ordinance of September 2025](2025-10-07-gabon-egov-legal-framework) makes interconnection between administrations compulsory and mandates digitisation of administrative services.
developments:
The ordinance on digitalisation and electronic government was signed by the President and published in the gazette of 7 September 2025, carrying compulsory interconnection between administrations and a national-preference clause in digital public procurement ([the ordinance](2025-10-07-gabon-egov-legal-framework)).

Its number comes from the minister's own commentary rather than from the instrument ([ministerial commentary](2025-10-24-gabon-2026-digital-budget-156pct)), and the base holds no article text or gazette reference.

It names no platform and no standard, so the obligation to interconnect exists without anything to interconnect through.

summary: An [ordinance of 8 April 2026](2026-07-26-gabonactu-apsad-libertes-civiques-numeriques-rapport-plaidoyer) regulating digital platforms is in force, its text unheld and its provisions judged disproportionate by the association reporting it.
developments:
The sole account of the ordinance is a civil-society advocacy report presented on 25 July 2026, which records it as in force and recommends its revision; no primary text, number or gazette citation is held ([advocacy report](2026-07-26-gabonactu-apsad-libertes-civiques-numeriques-rapport-plaidoyer)).

A separate civil-society declaration states that a social-media regulation bill exists and awaits promulgation, giving no title, number or adoption date, and it may be the same instrument ([declaration](2026-07-13-gabon-social-media-suspension)).

The base therefore holds two accounts of platform regulation and no instrument behind either.

summary: A [communications authority decision](2026-07-13-gabon-social-media-suspension) suspending social media has run about five months with no lifting date given.
developments:
The decision was in force until further notice as at 17 July 2026, about five months after it was taken, and the decision text is not held ([suspension](2026-07-13-gabon-social-media-suspension)).

The Presidency describes it as temporary and conservatory ([presidential framing](2026-07-19-gabonreview-suspension-reseaux-sociaux-mesure-temporaire)), while nine civil-society organisations call it unconstitutional and beyond the authority's remit and demand its abrogation ([advocacy report](2026-07-26-gabonactu-apsad-libertes-civiques-numeriques-rapport-plaidoyer)).

February 2026 is inferred from a five-month count and independently from an operator's half-year filing, so the start is held to the month ([operator filing](2026-07-22-maroc-telecom-rapport-financier-semestriel-2026)).

summary: The telecommunications regulator [established a standing tripartite forum](2026-08-21-lunion-gabon-arcep-tripartite-dialogue) in August 2026, bringing consumers into regulation alongside itself and the operators.
developments:
The dialogue space was established at Libreville on 20 August 2026 ([dialogue committee](2026-08-20-agp-gabon-arcep-dialogue-committee)) and is the first structured route for consumers into telecommunications regulation the base holds ([tripartite forum](2026-08-21-lunion-gabon-arcep-tripartite-dialogue)).

No terms of reference, meeting cadence or membership list is published, so what is recorded is the establishment and not the participation.

summary: At a departmental capital the incumbent [sells data bundles on a network whose coverage comes and goes](2026-08-25-depeches241-gabon-mbigou-moov-africa-reseau-arcep) while validity runs down normally.
developments:
Reporting of 25 August 2026 sets out prepaid credit and bundle validity running against a service that intermittently is not there, and puts the regulator's inaction to the president of its regulatory council ([service quality](2026-08-25-depeches241-gabon-mbigou-moov-africa-reseau-arcep)).

No regulator decision, quality-of-service determination or sanction is published, so the obligation is asserted in reporting and nowhere else in the base.

summary: A [candidacy for telecommunications union governance bodies](2026-07-31-gabon-digital-transformation-review) is under review, alongside participation in the African digital ministers' council.
developments:
The candidacy was reviewed at the ministry's final technical committee of the administrative year, with no body, seat, slate or election date named ([technical committee](2026-07-31-gabon-digital-transformation-review)).

That is the whole of the record on multilateral policy engagement, and the base holds no position under the African Union convention on cyber security and personal data protection.

The central bank adopted a regional financial inclusion strategy for 2025-2029 covering the six member states, validated by the monetary union's ministerial committee on 21 December 2023 and published in February 2025 ([strategy](2025-02-01-beac-strategie-regionale-inclusion-financiere-cemac)); the base holds no member-state implementation plan, target or outturn under it.

summary: A draft Code of Civil Procedure would [harmonise national procedure with the regional uniform acts](2026-08-12-gabon-code-procedure-civile-digitalisation), rewriting a 1977 ordinance.
developments:
A justice ministry commission submitted a draft running to more than 800 pages on 11 August 2026, aligning national civil procedure with the regional business-law uniform acts ([draft code](2026-08-12-gabon-code-procedure-civile-digitalisation)).

The draft text is not held and no timetable for consultation or introduction is stated, with professional consultation and parliamentary debate still ahead.

summary: [Three accords with Equatorial Guinea](2025-11-13-gabon-guinea-ecuatorial-fibra-roaming-frecuencias-techafricanews) were signed in November 2025 on fibre interconnection, free roaming and radio-frequency coordination.
developments:
The two digital-economy ministers signed at Mongomo on 13 November 2025 ([the accords](2025-11-13-gabon-guinea-ecuatorial-fibra-roaming-frecuencias-techafricanews)).

No commencement date, link capacity, tariff or coordination schedule is published, so what is held is three signatures and nothing about what has run under them since.

summary: A [regional health-data roadmap](2026-08-21-lunion-africa-cdc-central-africa-health-data-sharing-roadmap) was adopted in August 2026, and an airport passenger-data system [entered its operational phase](2026-08-14-gabon-api-pnr-airport-security-data).
developments:
The roadmap for cross-border health-data sharing among nine Central African states was adopted at a Libreville workshop of 18 to 21 August 2026, setting a six-week deadline for drafting an inter-country convention and a four-week deadline for a formal sharing mechanism, to be put to the health ministers of the seven states yet to sign the protocol ([roadmap](2026-08-21-lunion-africa-cdc-central-africa-health-data-sharing-roadmap)).

The advance passenger and passenger-name-record system moved into its operational phase on 14 August 2026 under the airport-security committee, with border risk-screening the stated purpose ([passenger data](2026-08-14-gabon-api-pnr-airport-security-data)).

Neither the roadmap nor the draft convention is published, and the convention terms, the retention rule for passenger data and any authorisation by the data-protection authority are not held.

progress: Advanced, on a proposal presented rather than an enacted appropriation
summary: The digital ministry's appropriation was [proposed at XAF 82bn for 2026](2025-10-24-gabon-2026-digital-budget-156pct), up 156.2 per cent on the XAF 32bn the minister recounts for 2025.
developments:
The proposal was presented to the National Transition Assembly across digital enterprise support, infrastructure deployment and digital literacy ([appropriation](2025-10-24-gabon-2026-digital-budget-156pct)).

The base holds no enacted finance law and no Gabonese source under this subject, and the 2025 comparator is a minister's own comparison rather than an appropriation document, so neither figure is confirmed against a budget instrument.

summary: A [card-network accord](2025-07-20-gabon-visa-partnership-public-services) of May 2025 and a [development fund partnership](2025-12-12-gabon-uncdf-financial-inclusion-deal) of December 2025 are both signed with no terms, amount or deliverable published.
developments:
The card-network accord was signed at a business forum in Abidjan on 12 and 13 May 2025 and reported second-hand, with one follow-up meeting on digitalising public services, tax collection, disbursement and secure digital identity ([card partnership](2025-07-20-gabon-visa-partnership-public-services)).

The development fund partnership covers policy support on financial governance aligned to the national plan and the regional financial inclusion strategy, with no money figure, duration or deliverable on file ([fund partnership](2025-12-12-gabon-uncdf-financial-inclusion-deal)).

Twelve months with no further record on the first, and nothing since December 2025 on the second, is the finding.

summary: A [credit-guarantee accord](2026-07-17-gabon-garantie-publique-huawei-start-up) and an [angel-network partnership](2026-08-20-agp-gabon-cgi-gain-startup-financing-mou) were signed for start-up finance in July and August 2026, both unquantified.
developments:
The guarantee accord was signed on the margins of a start-up programme launch to reduce the risk borne by institutions lending to innovative young firms, with no ceiling, coverage ratio, eligibility test, term, participating bank or envelope published ([guarantee accord](2026-07-17-gabon-garantie-publique-huawei-start-up)).

The national innovation centre and a domestic angel investor network sealed a partnership on 20 August 2026 to ease start-up access to financing, with no fund size, pipeline or first investment published ([angel partnership](2026-08-20-agp-gabon-cgi-gain-startup-financing-mou)).

Against those, the one closed instrument is a guarantee of US$27,630,000 covering an equity investment in a mobile-money operator, whose guarantee period has ended ([closed guarantee](2022-01-01-miga-gab-airtel-mobile-money-2022-airtel-mobile-money-gabon-digital-financial)).

summary: The [Digital Gabon Project](2026-02-24-gabon-digital-reform-execution-speedup) has disbursed about US$13.4m of US$68.5m, its original closing date passed with no closure or extension on file.
developments:
Disbursement stood at US$13,419,063 of US$68.5m on the project portal, against US$1.3m and all results indicators at baseline in December 2024 ([earlier reading](2024-12-19-world-bank-digital-gabon-isr-seq7), [project](2021-07-30-wb-gab-001-digital-gabon-project)).

The ministry put the rate at 7 per cent of FCFA 44bn in February 2026, up from 3 per cent, and the mid-term review planned for October 2025 is not on file ([execution](2026-02-24-gabon-digital-reform-execution-speedup)).

The earlier health project entered its closure phase, reviewed in June 2026 with no closure date or outcome rating held ([closure review](2026-06-22-gabon-aninf-worldbank-progress-review)), and the backbone financing closed against US$23m committed, with no successor on file ([backbone](2016-06-29-wb-gab-002-additional-financing-cab4)).

summary: [2,000 km of backbone](2026-07-27-agp-gabon-communications-spatiales-11-recommandations-souverainete) is deployed, with 88 per cent forest cover cited as the physical limit on extending it further.
developments:
The figure is ministry-stated at a satellite seminar in July 2026 rather than a regulator or operator return, and extension works are said to be under way ([backbone](2026-07-27-agp-gabon-communications-spatiales-11-recommandations-souverainete)).

On access, the incumbent announced nine new fibre-to-the-home localities for 2025 on top of eight opened in 2024, and the base holds a plan and never a completion ([access programme](2025-01-29-gabon-moov-ftth-coverage-leader)).

The first technology-neutral fixed authorisation was signed with the regulator in January 2025 carrying no build obligation or coverage target, and nothing is on record of what has been built under it since ([fixed authorisation](2025-01-07-gabon-airtel-fixed-services)).

summary: The exchange point [passed 250 Mbps of local traffic](2026-05-13-gabon-gabix-ixp-relaunch) after the two mobile operators reconnected, from about 80 Mbps and two members.
developments:
The two operators reconnected on 13 May 2026 and local traffic passed 250 Mbps, against about 80 Mbps unchanged since 2019 on two members ([relaunch](2026-05-13-gabon-gabix-ixp-relaunch)).

A national reboot workshop ran from 3 to 8 August 2026 with an international internet body and the regional registry, closing with certificates after six days of peering, security and sovereignty training ([reboot workshop](2026-08-08-gabon-gabix-reboot-workshop-interconnection), [workshop programme](2026-08-03-gabix-reboot-atelier-national-peering-gabon)).

The registry called for a network of trained ambassadors to carry the skills into firms and administrations, and operator representatives named broader institutional buy-in as the remaining task; the post-relaunch member count has not been published.

summary: The regulator [prohibited the sale, installation and use](2026-05-19-le360-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux) of one satellite service in May 2026 on penalty of fines, imprisonment and equipment seizure.
developments:
The prohibition follows a warning against illegal commercialisation issued in November 2025 ([regulator warning](2025-11-06-gabon-arcep-met-en-garde-commercialisation-illegale-starlink)), and was announced with nationwide enforcement controls.

At the same date the operator's own map still listed the country as available from 2026, with no licence granted ([prohibition](2026-05-19-le360-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux)).

No enforcement outcome is on file: no seizure, fine or prosecution has been reported, and no authorised satellite broadband provider exists on the record.

summary: [92 racks and 1 MW](2026-07-07-gabon-datacenter-inauguration-figures) entered service in July 2026, against about 95 per cent of national data previously hosted abroad.
developments:
The country had no data centre in service before July 2026; 92 racks and 1 MW went live on 3 July, with a further 160 racks and over 1 MW due end-November to early-December 2026 ([capacity](2026-07-07-gabon-datacenter-inauguration-figures), [second facility](2026-07-31-gabon-datacenter-tier-iii-avancement-chantier)).

About 95 per cent of data produced in the country is hosted outside it, reported by the operator that built the alternative, with no independent measurement held ([hosting share](2026-07-07-gabon-datacenter-inauguration-figures)).

Utilisation is published at neither site.

summary: A [first national facility was inaugurated](2026-07-07-gabon-datacenter-inauguration-figures) at a special economic zone in July 2026, and a state-owned second is under construction.
developments:
The first facility carries 92 racks over 3,000 square metres and 1 MW installed at XAF 8bn, peered to two submarine systems, after delivery slipped twice from the groundbreaking of August 2025 ([inauguration](2026-07-07-gabon-datacenter-inauguration-figures), [specification](2026-07-08-gabon-sovereign-datacenter-technical-spec)).

A state company is building the second, with 160 racks and over 1 MW, commissioning stated for end-November to early-December 2026 and no cost published ([site inspection](2026-07-31-gabon-datacenter-tier-iii-avancement-chantier)).

Two other arrangements have produced nothing: a national data centre convention signed before the President in June 2025 still has no site, cost, capacity or timeline thirteen months on ([convention](2025-06-29-gabon-lunion-national-datacenter)), and a framework memorandum on secure infrastructure, cloud and digital identity has no workplan, value or deliverable published ([framework memorandum](2025-07-16-gabon-aninf-st-digital-mou)).

summary: A photovoltaic plant supplies [about 22 per cent of site energy](2026-07-08-gabon-sovereign-datacenter-technical-spec) at the new data centre, with water-free cooling and a dual redundant feed.
developments:
The design announced in February 2025 promised partial solar supply, adiabatic cooling and rainwater recycling ([announcement](2025-02-14-gabon-st-digital-nkok-datacenter-announced)); what entered service is a plant covering about 22 per cent of need, water-free cooling and a dual 15 kV feed with redundant units ([specification](2026-07-08-gabon-sovereign-datacenter-technical-spec)).

The share is operator-stated rather than metered, and power usage effectiveness is not published ([inauguration figures](2026-07-07-gabon-datacenter-inauguration-figures)).

The base holds no grid supply position for data-centre load at either site.

summary: An [information-systems audit of the health insurance fund](2026-08-13-gabon-aninf-cnamgs-partenariat-numerique) was delivered in August 2026, three months after the memorandum that commissioned it.
developments:
The memorandum was signed in May 2026 ([memorandum](2026-05-10-gabon-cnamgs-aninf-mou)) and the findings were delivered on 12 August, naming human resources, data and infrastructure as the three pillars of the fund's technology roadmap ([audit delivery](2026-08-13-gabon-aninf-cnamgs-partenariat-numerique)).

The findings themselves are not published, and no remediation plan, timetable or cost is stated. It is the only audit of a government system the base holds, and there is no workforce measure for information and communications technology anywhere in it.

progress: Mixed, an architecture and an asset inventory are being built while no strategy exists and a utility lost most of its systems
summary: [No national strategy is published](2026-01-25-gabon-cybersecurity-ai-soft-power-hub), and a June 2026 attack collapsed 95 per cent of a utility's information systems.
developments:
A national cybersecurity strategy was named as an objective of the second national forum, by a vendor rather than by the agency or the ministry, and a regulator workshop of January 2026 restated resilience gaps without producing one ([forum](2025-11-20-gabon-2nd-cybersecurity-forum), [workshop](2026-01-25-gabon-cybersecurity-ai-soft-power-hub)).

A security bill of material launched in June 2025 has published no asset count, coverage, review cycle or output in the fourteen months since, and its stated linkage target, a national security operations centre and incident response team, is not established anywhere in the base ([method](2025-06-01-gabon-aninf-secbom-cybersecurity)).

A national cybersecurity architecture is in design with twelve priority sectors defined and a strategic-asset inventory being mapped, on a single trade account with no counterparty primary on file ([architecture](2026-06-23-gabon-aninf-mitre-cybersecurity)).

A sabotage attack on 15 June 2026 collapsed 95 per cent of the electricity utility's systems and knocked out prepaid-meter top-up ([recovery](2026-08-06-gabon-seeg-cyberattack-systems-recovery)). Billing and payment were restored in the capital and seven interior centres by 4 August, on the company's own statement, with no forensic or damage-cost report on file.

A regional police operation concluded in August 2025 with 1,209 arrests and about US$97.4m recovered across eighteen countries, none of it attributed to Gabon ([operation](2025-08-26-gabon-cybercrime-interpol-recovery)).

summary: The indicator for [five government entities exchanging data securely](2024-12-19-world-bank-digital-gabon-isr-seq7) stands at its zero baseline, and the platform itself is unnamed.
developments:
No value has been published above the zero baseline recorded in December 2024, and no entity is exchanging data on the record ([project indicator](2024-12-19-world-bank-digital-gabon-isr-seq7)).

The ordinance of September 2025 makes interconnection between administrations compulsory but names no platform and no standard, so the obligation has nothing to run through ([the ordinance](2025-10-07-gabon-egov-legal-framework)).

summary: [335,384 people have enrolled](2026-06-03-gabon-cnie-enrolment-figures-assembly) for the electronic identity card since June 2024, with 147,224 cards collected and 78,500 files disputed.
developments:
The first public coverage figures were given to the National Assembly on 2 June 2026: 335,384 enrolled, 164,944 cards produced, 147,224 collected, 92,614 files in processing and 78,500 disputed ([enrolment figures](2026-06-03-gabon-cnie-enrolment-figures-assembly)).

Issuance launched on 24 June 2024 ([launch](2024-06-26-gabon-launches-electronic-national-id-card)) with no enrolment figure on the record and the project indicator still at a zero baseline ([project indicator](2024-12-19-world-bank-digital-gabon-isr-seq7)).

The disputed files are about 23 per cent of all enrolments ([disputed files](2026-06-03-gabon-cnie-enrolment-figures-assembly)), and the count rests on press accounts of a spoken answer; no registry or ministry publication exists.

summary: The national directorate [enrols, personalises and issues in-house](2024-01-01-in-groupe-insight-report-2023-24) at its own facility, with a foreign supplier providing the card and the software.
developments:
The supplier's own annual review lists the card and passport among its delivered solutions, and it is the only primary on the question ([supplier review](2024-01-01-in-groupe-insight-report-2023-24)).

The directorate personalises in-house alongside the passport and the residence permit, which is what reporting means when it describes the card as produced domestically; the two layers are compatible and were once read as three competing suppliers.

No procurement notice, award publication or gazette entry is held, so the supply arrangement is established by the supplier's own publication and by no Gabonese public record.

summary: Two registers have been [opened as workshops and never built](2025-06-23-gabon-legal-digital-id-three-projects): a biometric register of natural persons and a national digital identity system.
developments:
The biometric register was seeded on the legacy civil registry and its implementation workshop opened in June 2025 with no build reported ([stocktake](2025-06-23-gabon-legal-digital-id-three-projects)).

The digital identity system's workshops opened at Ntoum under the donor-financed digital project, and the last mention is a governance-day framing of 16 September 2025 ([governance day](2025-09-16-gabon-digital-identity-governance-milestone)).

Fourteen months of the window have passed with no build, pilot or delivery date published for either.

summary: The [biometric civil registry](2012-09-20-gemalto-gabon-biometric-national-registry) has operated since 2012 and remains the seed base for the register that would replace it.
developments:
It was built under a supplier contract of September 2012 ([the registry](2012-09-20-gemalto-gabon-biometric-national-registry)) and is named as an existing system in the 2025 stocktake of legal identity ([stocktake](2025-06-23-gabon-legal-digital-id-three-projects)).

No registration count, coverage figure, birth-registration rate or interoperability arrangement is held for it, so what is recorded is that it operates and nothing about how much of the population it holds.

summary: An [electoral-roll verification platform](2025-01-01-gabon-electoral-roll-verification-platform) is live for the 2025 cycle, keyed on the personal identification number.
developments:
The platform was published by the digital agency for the electoral cycle and lets a voter check the roll against the identification number ([verification platform](2025-01-01-gabon-electoral-roll-verification-platform)).

No usage figure is published at either end of the window, no register size is held, and the source page is undated so the position carries year precision only.

summary: A [single file of state participations](2026-01-14-gabon-public-finance-egov-initiatives) was reported established in January 2026 to centralise data on the state's shareholdings.
developments:
It was stated established at the ministerial session of 13 January 2026 ([ministerial session](2026-01-14-gabon-public-finance-egov-initiatives)).

The account is a single secondary one, and no register, scope, publication or operator is held, so nothing establishes what it contains or who keeps it. The base holds no commercial business register at all.

summary: A [proposal for an integrated urban land management system](2025-12-02-gabon-cadastre-digitalisation-land-title) was submitted in December 2025, against about 1,200 cession decisions signed that year.
developments:
The proposal was submitted with drone purchases announced alongside it, and no system, contract award or delivery date is held ([cadastre proposal](2025-12-02-gabon-cadastre-digitalisation-land-title), [modernisation](2025-11-24-gabon-cadastre-modernization-ign-fi)).

Ministers told public television on 30 November 2025 that about 1,200 cession decisions were signed in 2025, with about 3,000 beneficiaries owing about FCFA 14bn in unpaid fees ([cession figures](2025-12-01-gabon-land-registry-cession-figures)).

A proposal was received rather than awarded, so no engagement, signature or value is established, and the cession figures are a television statement rather than a register return.

summary: The [unified social register](2026-07-29-agp-gabon-registre-social-unifie-rsug-premier-livrable) presented its first deliverable in July 2026, and a second census of the economically weak begins fieldwork in September.
developments:
Technical work was finalised at a closing workshop in August 2025 with nothing delivered ([technical close](2025-08-28-gabon-registre-social-unique)); the first deliverable was presented at Libreville in July 2026 alongside a commitment to full digitalisation of non-contributory social protection under the national plan ([first deliverable](2026-07-29-agp-gabon-registre-social-unifie-rsug-premier-livrable)).

An interministerial committee fixed the terms of a second census of economically weak citizens in July 2026, with fieldwork from September drawing on the population census and health-insurance records, because the existing social file is not reliable enough to target protection ([census terms](2026-07-21-gabonreview-recensement-gabonais-economiquement-faibles)).

The state's own source uses three different names for the register, and no beneficiary count, coverage or platform is published.

summary: A [regional interoperable QR standard](2026-07-30-gabonreview-beac-qr-code-interoperable-cemac) took effect under an April 2026 regulation, routed through the regional switch with the Gabonese scheme as its pilot.
developments:
The standard was launched at Douala under a regional monetary union regulation of 8 April 2026 and is in force across the six member states, settled through the regional switch ([standard](2026-07-30-cemac-gimac-norme-qr-code-interoperable)).

Merchant-presented mode is the primary mode, explicitly to avoid the capital cost of terminals ([launch](2026-07-30-gabonreview-beac-qr-code-interoperable-cemac)).

The national scheme is the pilot for it, which is the base's only evidence of the central bank shaping domestic payments rather than the region setting the rule.

summary: The regional central bank [acceded to the pan-African settlement system](2026-07-10-beac-joins-papss-cemac-banks-agenceecofin) in July 2026, against a target of connecting member-state banks by end-2026.
developments:
Accession was announced with integration work not started on the record ([accession](2026-07-10-beac-joins-papss-cemac-banks-agenceecofin)).

Within the region the two Gabonese mobile-money operators lead issuing: one first with 1,969,325 transactions worth FCFA 68.1bn in the first half of 2026 and the other second with 1,950,401 transactions worth FCFA 55.8bn ([issuing position](2026-07-30-ga-moov-gabon-premier-emetteur-paiements-cemac)). On acquiring, the first is third behind two Cameroonian operators, with 758,629 transactions ([the same figures](2026-07-30-ga-moov-gabon-premier-emetteur-paiements-cemac)).

The figures are those the outlet states it consulted, and no publication by the regional switch is held.

summary: A [national QR payment scheme](2025-12-11-gabon-madigipaie-digital-payments-launch) launched in December 2025 with more than 1,000 codes, and the regional switch moved 20.3m transactions in 2025.
developments:
The scheme was launched at Libreville by the regional switch operator, presided over by the central bank governor, with more than 1,000 codes at launch ([launch](2025-12-09-gimac-madigipaie-lancement-libreville), [scheme](2025-12-11-gabon-madigipaie-digital-payments-launch)).

It extended to the taxi network on 28 February 2026 ([taxi extension](2026-03-01-gabon-madigipaie-taxigab)) and municipal facilitation was agreed on 3 July 2026 ([municipal agreement](2026-07-07-gabon-lunion-madigipaie-libreville)); no transaction volume, value or merchant count above the launch codes has been published since.

The regional switch itself carried 20.3m transactions worth FCFA 863bn across 153 participants in 2025, against a reconstructed 14.5m worth about FCFA 710bn in 2024 ([switch figures](2026-07-30-cemac-gimacpay-transactions-2025)).

summary: [4.5m mobile-money accounts of which 1.6m active](2025-12-11-gabon-madigipaie-digital-payments-launch) at end-2024 remain the base's current statement, against 457,377 cardholders.
developments:
The ministry's end-2024 figures were cited at a payment launch in December 2025 and nothing later has been published: 368.3m transactions worth FCFA 4,087bn in 2024, against FCFA 3,487bn in 2023 ([accounts](2025-12-11-gabon-madigipaie-digital-payments-launch)).

On cards, the bank association reports 457,377 cardholders among 673,793 bank clients at end-June 2026, against 326 cash machines and 1,535 merchant terminals ([card estate](2026-07-30-ga-cartes-bancaires-paiements-tpe)). Of 1,101,434 transactions in June, 62.41 per cent were cash withdrawals and 24.61 per cent terminal payments ([the same return](2026-07-30-ga-cartes-bancaires-paiements-tpe)).

A terminal estate 4.7 times the size of the cash-machine estate carries under half its traffic, on industry-reported figures.

summary: At least [80 per cent of tax revenue](2025-09-15-gabon-2026-budget-revenue-digitalization) is collected through the revenue platform, and an online declaration portal went live in 2025.
developments:
The tax authority's 2024 report puts at least 80 per cent of revenue through the system, live since April 2024, and no later share has been published ([revenue platform](2025-09-15-gabon-2026-budget-revenue-digitalization)).

An online declaration and payment portal was announced live by the authority in August 2025 ([portal](2025-08-18-gabon-etax-dgi-portal-launch)).

The share is self-reported by the authority, and the base holds no electronic invoicing mandate and no national platform for the payment and collection of public revenue beyond the tax system.

summary: The health information system is [still at thirteen pilot facilities](2025-07-29-gabon-egabon-sis-health-mis-equipment), equipped in a second phase and with no national extension published.
developments:
Second-phase equipment was handed to the thirteen pilot facilities in July 2025 and the count has not moved since ([pilot equipment](2025-07-29-gabon-egabon-sis-health-mis-equipment)).

No facility count beyond the pilots, interconnection figure or national deployment plan is published, and the project that funds it entered its closure phase in June 2026 with no outcome rating held.

summary: The education management system [took delivery of 1,000 tablets](2026-07-30-agp-gabon-1000-tablettes-education-unicef-banque-mondiale) in July 2026 for the 148 schools recorded as connected.
developments:
School-health and well-being indicators were integrated into the system from August 2025 ([indicator integration](2025-08-09-gabon-school-health-sige-integration)), on a base where school data collection had been named a priority earlier that year ([data collection](2025-03-11-gabon-school-data-collection-priority)).

The education minister gave 148 connected schools at the tablet handover, the first published count the base holds and with no denominator given ([tablet handover](2026-07-30-agp-gabon-1000-tablettes-education-unicef-banque-mondiale)).

The tablets are a teaching input and the base does not connect them to the system.

summary: A draft Code of Civil Procedure would [introduce digitised procedural filings](2026-08-12-gabon-code-procedure-civile-digitalisation) and secure digital tools, replacing a 1977 ordinance.
developments:
A justice ministry commission submitted a draft of more than 800 pages on 11 August 2026, rewriting the ordinance to allow paperless filings ([draft code](2026-08-12-gabon-code-procedure-civile-digitalisation)).

On the custodial side, a standardised model of custody register was presented at a national roundtable in February 2025 and digitalisation was explored, with paper registers accepted as a first step ([custody registers](2025-02-01-gabon-custody-registers-judicial-safeguards)).

Nothing dated has followed on the registers since February 2025, and the draft code's text, consultation timetable and introduction date are all unheld.

summary: A [public finance system went live](2026-01-18-gabon-sigfip-public-finance-platform-launch) and connected to the Treasury, while a single window and an internal civil-service suite remain presentations.
developments:
The public finance system was launched following a presidential directive of October 2025, is live and connected to the Treasury, and national and overseas-post extension is stated as intended, with no transaction volume or coverage figure published ([public finance system](2026-01-18-gabon-sigfip-public-finance-platform-launch)).

A single digital window was presented to the President by the same supplier in February 2026, with no build stage, launch date, budget or procurement record held ([single window](2026-02-20-gabon-connect-single-digital-window)).

An integrated suite for secure messaging and confidential document exchange between civil servants was presented in August 2026, built with a domestic start-up and with the state holding the source code at no cost; deployment follows a ministry-by-ministry review of procedures and no rollout date is published ([civil-service suite](2026-08-04-gabon-le-gouvernement-sassocie-au-cgi-pour-la-plateforme-administration-ga)).

A tourist electronic visa platform operates for a three-month free visa, with no volumes, processing times or window dates published ([visa platform](2026-08-02-gabon-e-visa-touristique-barrieres-administratives)).

2026-08-31 — a government services portal is in pilot preparation, the government secretariat having [opened interministerial consultations in June 2026 across five ministries with at least ten services to be integrated by December](2026-08-31-wearetech-gabon-rwanda-digital-transformation). The base does not state whether this is the single digital window already on the ledger or a second instrument, and no budget or supplier is published.

summary: The digital agency [opened its first provincial office](2026-06-24-gabon-aninf-franceville-office) in June 2026, fifteen years after it was created with nothing outside the capital.
developments:
The office was inaugurated at Franceville, the agency's first outside Libreville since its creation in 2011 ([provincial office](2026-06-24-gabon-aninf-franceville-office)).

The account is a trade rewrite and no staffing, budget or service figure is given, so the base records one office and nothing about what it does.

progress: No change, a first mention with nothing measured behind it
summary: The capital's mayor states the city [already operates its own revenue-digitalisation system](2026-07-07-gabon-lunion-madigipaie-libreville), developed with the Treasury and distinct from the national scheme.
developments:
The statement was made when the national payment scheme reached municipal facilitation, and the mayor was explicit that the national scheme will not replace the city's own ([mayor's statement](2026-07-07-gabon-lunion-madigipaie-libreville)).

The system is unnamed and undated, with no coverage or revenue figure, and it is the only subnational records system the base holds.

summary: A [protocol with Morocco](2026-04-13-techafricanews-morocco-gabon-digital-skills) of April 2026 covers exchange of artificial-intelligence expertise and digital skills, with no budget, term or workplan.
developments:
It was signed as an outcome of a technology exhibition at Marrakech in April 2026 and is the only instrument in the base whose stated subject is artificial intelligence ([protocol](2026-04-13-techafricanews-morocco-gabon-digital-skills)).

No national artificial-intelligence strategy or policy, no compute capacity and no register of deployed systems or use cases exists anywhere in the base, so the protocol names a subject the country has no domestic instrument for.

summary: A [ride-hailing platform began recruiting drivers](2026-08-19-gabonreview-yango-libreville-transport-urbain) at Libreville in August 2026, entering a market one competitor has held since 2021.
developments:
The platform works as a pure intermediary with no fleet or drivers of its own, in partnership with a local transport operator, and has announced no launch date, cities, tariffs or regulatory framework ([market entry](2026-08-19-gabonreview-yango-libreville-transport-urbain)).

Electric taxis were deployed in late 2025 under a state-backed project, and no regulatory framework for the entry is stated. The base holds no measure of the digital sector's economic weight against which to read any of it.

summary: The [state digital incubator lost its director general and its premises](2026-08-24-gabonreview-sing-sa-dg-limoge-projet-fusion-cgi) in August 2026, with a merger into the innovation centre under study.
developments:
The director general was removed at a board meeting while he was abroad, the head office has been emptied with no new address announced, and the interim passed to a deputy of the state holding that owns 30% of the incubator's capital ([incubator](2026-08-24-gabonreview-sing-sa-dg-limoge-projet-fusion-cgi)).

Its claimed record since 2018 is 314 startups supported, about FCFA 550m mobilised and a 68% post-incubation survival rate ([incubator](2026-08-24-gabonreview-sing-sa-dg-limoge-projet-fusion-cgi)), and no ministerial statement of its future is on file.

Against that, a memorandum signed at the data-centre inauguration is to give ministry-supported start-ups professional hosting at preferential rates, with no rate, eligibility list or take-up figure published ([hosting memorandum](2026-07-06 Gabon Inaugurates First Tier III Datacenter to Boost Digital Sovereignty)).

summary: A [national start-up accelerator launched](2026-07-14-kimba-connect-gabon) in July 2026 reports 155 registrations and 66 shortlisted, its final pushed to the autumn.
developments:
The programme launched with the employers' federation offering finance, technology, labelling and market access, on organisers' estimates of 150 to 200 start-ups in the country ([launch](2026-07-14-kimba-connect-gabon)).

The final set for 4 August was postponed on 6 August after participating start-ups objected to how the edition was organised ([postponement](2026-08-06-gabon-postpones-kimba-connect-finale-following-startup-concerns)), and a revised agenda published on 11 August runs pitches to 24 August and moves the final to late September or early October ([revised agenda](2026-08-11-gabon-kimba-connect-preselection-agenda)).

The accelerator reports 155 registered start-ups, 133 of which submitted against 16 published challenges, and 66 shortlisted, all its own figures with no laureate list or selection criteria held ([revised agenda](2026-08-11-gabon-kimba-connect-preselection-agenda)).

A Start-up and Digital Enterprise Act is named as forthcoming by the minister, with no bill, gazetted text or timetable, and no Gabonese primary names it ([the Act](2026-02-10 Why Africa should sequence not rush into AI)).

summary: A [draft decree creating a basic computing and internet certificate](2026-07-24-agp-gabon-textes-application-digitalisation-des-enseignements) was validated in July 2026, with no syllabus, awarding body or start date.
developments:
The decree was validated at a national workshop on the digitalisation of teaching and forwarded to the competent authorities ([validated texts](2026-07-24-agp-gabon-textes-application-digitalisation-des-enseignements)).

It is a draft only, and the base holds no named national digital-literacy programme, no literacy measure and no cohort target against which to read it.

summary: [Five implementing texts on digitalised teaching](2026-07-24-agp-gabon-textes-application-digitalisation-des-enseignements) were validated by consensus in July 2026 and forwarded to the competent authorities.
developments:
The five are two decrees, on digitalised learning and on blended-learning platforms, two orders, on assessment and on the steering committee, and a decree creating the basic computing certificate ([validated texts](2026-07-24-agp-gabon-textes-application-digitalisation-des-enseignements)).

They are validated technically and not adopted, and neither the parent ordinance nor the law ratifying it is held, so the texts rest on an instrument the base cannot read.

summary: The Constitutional Court [moved to field verification of the population census](2026-08-21-gabonreview-rgpl-cour-constitutionnelle-verification-chiffres) across all nine provinces before deciding whether to certify it.
developments:
The Court heard the planning minister on 12 August 2026 and then deployed teams to test the reliability of the figures; in one province the governor reported enumeration coverage above 95% and asked for more river and sea transport to reach remote populations ([verification](2026-08-21-gabonreview-rgpl-cour-constitutionnelle-verification-chiffres)).

A second census, of economically weak citizens, has its terms fixed and fieldwork from September 2026, drawing on the population census and health-insurance records ([second census](2026-07-21-gabonreview-recensement-gabonais-economiquement-faibles)).

Certification of the definitive results awaits the Court's analysis, so no certified population figure is established.

summary: The only statistical-capacity finance the base holds [closed against US$50m committed](2017-03-30-wb-gab-004-gabon-statistical-development-project), with no successor operation.
developments:
The project was committed in 2017 and closed in 2023, before the window opened, and nothing has replaced it ([statistical project](2017-03-30-wb-gab-004-gabon-statistical-development-project)).

No national strategy for the development of statistics, no statistical office output and no successor capacity operation is on file, so the census now under judicial verification is being run without any of them recorded.

summary: An external assessment judged the country [not to meet minimum fiscal transparency requirements](2026-08-19-gabonreview-transparence-fiscale-us-fiscal-transparency-report-2026) again in its 2026 report.
developments:
The 2026 report, published on 11 August 2026 for the review period to 31 December 2025, presses governments to publish and regularly update information on state financial obligations including those of major state-owned enterprises; of 139 governments and one entity reviewed, 73 met the requirements and 67 did not, 14 of the latter judged to have made significant progress ([assessment](2026-08-19-gabonreview-transparence-fiscale-us-fiscal-transparency-report-2026)).

The previous review found only limited information published on debt obligations, excluding state-owned enterprise debt, no timely publication of the executive budget proposal or end-of-year report, and quarterly execution reports judged limited and unreliable. The base holds no open government data portal or policy.

summary: A [cybersecurity grant](2024-01-01-state-gab-cybersecurity-gabon-2024-cybersecurity-in-gabon) has disbursed US$49,313 of US$1,249,997 past its planned end date, and certification training runs at the embassy's cultural centre.
developments:
The grant was committed in 2024 against a planned end of 22 December 2025; that date has passed with no completion, extension or further disbursement on file, leaving disbursement at 3.9 per cent of commitment on the only reading the base holds ([grant](2024-01-01-state-gab-cybersecurity-gabon-2024-cybersecurity-in-gabon)).

Networking-academy certification training is under way at Libreville's American Corner under a digital-skills programme, with no cohort size or completion date published ([training](2026-08-11-cybastion-us-embassies-digital-skills-africa)), against a commitment first announced in June 2025 with no cohort, curriculum, start date or delivery partner ([announcement](2025-06-29-gabon-lunion-national-datacenter)).

Separately, advanced talks at about US$9bn were reported for the acquisition of a satellite operator holding spectrum authorisations and partnerships in the country, in a single secondary excerpt with no licence or counterparty named ([acquisition talks](2026-04-14 Amazon's $9bn satellite deal set to benefit Africa)).

summary: A [digital transformation memorandum](2026-01-05 Gabon and Huawei Forge Partnership to Boost National Digital Transformation) signed in December 2025 is in force on three pillars, and a skills accord followed in July 2026.
developments:
An exploratory ministerial mission to the supplier's sites in June 2025 produced no agreement ([exploration](2025-07-01-gabon-huawei-partnership-exploration)); the memorandum was signed on 23 December 2025 on a joint project committee, integration of Gabonese start-ups and skills transfer, with the connected-schools programme to expand from 2026 ([memorandum](2026-01-05 Gabon and Huawei Forge Partnership to Boost National Digital Transformation)).

The skills accord of 14 July 2026 has the supplier create smart rooms, run training in networks, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and software development, and give access to its certifying kits, with no room count, trainee target, cost or duration published ([skills accord](2026-07-17-gabon-garantie-publique-huawei-start-up), [programme launch](2026-07-14-kimba-connect-gabon)); curriculum, certificate and equipment all belong to one vendor.

A smart-cities memorandum recorded for 2024 remains at pipeline status with at least US$234m pledged and nothing drawn, the single largest line in the country's finance aggregate and reaching the base through two secondary hops ([smart cities](2024-01-01-huawei-gab-2024-gabon-smart-cities-mou-bw01)).
